items.title: PixelPerfect Web Exploitation Write-up
items.summary:
TL;DR PixelPerfect Web Exploitation Write-up is a misc challenge from tmp. This challenge exposes a Sinatra-based image processing application that accepts two main inputs: Summary This challenge exposes a Sinatra-based image processing application that accepts two main inputs:
image file uploaded by the user transformation metadata in key: value format The main vulnerability lies in the use of instance_eval against strings constructed directly from user metadata. Even though the application tries to apply a simple blacklist to the metadata, the implementation still allows Ruby code injection via the directive or key metadata section.
items.content_html:
TL;DR
PixelPerfect Web Exploitation Write-up is a misc challenge from tmp. This challenge exposes a Sinatra-based image processing application that accepts two main inputs:

Summary

This challenge exposes a Sinatra-based image processing application that accepts two main inputs:

  1. image file uploaded by the user
  2. transformation metadata in key: value format

The main vulnerability lies in the use of instance_eval against strings constructed directly from user metadata. Even though the application tries to apply a simple blacklist to the metadata, the implementation still allows Ruby code injection via the directive or key metadata section.

items.title: Broken Chain – CTF Writeup
items.summary: TL;DR Broken Chain – CTF Writeup is a misc challenge from HackerDNA. This writeup provides a complete walkthrough and technical analysis. Overview The Broken Chain challenge demonstrates how multiple small vulnerabilities can be chained together to achieve full system compromise. The exploitation path includes a Zip Slip vulnerability, remote command execution, interaction with an internal backup service, credential disclosure, and finally privilege escalation via a misconfigured sudo rule allowing Vim execution as root.
